glosses: to add up, to sum up
Additionner, totaliser, calculer la somme de plusieurs éléments.

examples.text: Wir sollten mal unsere monatlichen Fixkosten zusammenrechnen.
Wenn man alles zusammenrechnet, ist die Fahrt mit der Bahn doch günstiger als ein Flug.

glosses: To take the sum of; to total.

examples.text: Add up the prices and find out how much it will cost.
When they added up the vaccine doses from all known and anticipate sources, they didn't have enough.
If you can save even a couple of dollars per day, it will add up to a lot over a year.
It all keeps adding up / I think I'm cracking up / Am I just paranoid? / Or am I just stoned?
The bus wound its way up into San Marino, passing through the various small castellos that add up to form the diminutive country, […]

glosses: To make sense; to be reasonable or consistent.

examples.text: His story just doesn't add up. Why would he have been at the restaurant the day before the event?

glosses: To calculate the sum of a number of numbers or quantities.

examples.text: As soon as Debbie can tot up the scores, we'll know who won.
Later, when Cora got a chance to tot up her sins for the day, she would vaguely recall hearing the protestors suddenly grow quiet and whisper to each other.
The bill tots up to 35 euros.

glosses: Ajouter plusieurs nombres l’un à l’autre pour en trouver le total.

examples.text: Il faut additionner toutes ces sommes.
Lucienne. — Quelle déception pour la pauvre femme qui a pu se croire distinguée et qui finit par s’apercevoir qu’elle n’est qu’additionnée.
Additionner de sucre un sirop. Ajouter du sucre.
Les enjeux s'additionnent.
Les probabilités de deux événements peuvent s'additionner sous certaines conditions.
